incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: Elevated RL rejects for org=planktonai detected. Spike in sustained QPS -> 480, 5xxs from inference nodes increasing. Alert: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/1768500123
Ryan (on-call): I'm on it, paging SRE. grabbing metrics now.
Liz (ops): seeing large prefix caching churn, a bunch of short requests. Probably client retry storm.
Maya (eng-sre): ETA 2m, can we apply temporary org-level limit bump to keep customer online? current org QPS=100, backpressure firing.
Ana (support): Customer reported degraded responses ~2m ago, CS ticket #CS-8243. They're on a paid dedicated plan and are seeing timeouts.
Ryan (on-call): OK propose: bump planktonai org QPS to 300 for 15m, enable token-based backoff (soft), and disable streaming for that org to reduce token overhead. Anyone object?
Liz (ops): +1. Also recommend disable non-essential realtime features (synthesis metrics) if quick.
Maya (eng-sre): I'll run the commands.
Ryan (on-call): running: ```bash
redwood rl adjust --org planktonai --qps 300 --window 15m --reason "emergency surge - reduce throttles"
```
incident-bot: action-log: rl.adjust executed by ryan ; org=planktonai ; from=100 ; to=300 ; window=15m ; id=rl-act-7612
Maya (eng-sre): toggling feature flag: ```bash
redwood ff set planktonai.streaming false --actor maya --note "reduce token churn during spike"
```
incident-bot: ff.update applied ; planktonai.streaming=false ; actor=maya ; id=ff-3849
Ana (support): Notifying customer in CS-8243: "We've temporarily increased your request limit and disabled streaming to stabilize your service. Monitoring closely; will follow up with details." :email: :white_check_mark:
Liz (ops): dashboards look better — 5xxs dropping, latency median down ~40%. QPS still high but within the bumped window.
Ryan (on-call): Good. Keep monitoring; if things stabilize we'll roll down early. If not, next step is to enable tiered routing fallback to smaller model.
Maya (eng-sre): adding short-term QoS rule to prefer low-latency pool for planktonai: ```yaml
# applied via infra-ui
org: planktonai
policy: prefer_low_latency
max_instances: 8
```
incident-bot: qos.apply queued -> success id=qos-9901
Ana (support): Customer acknowledges the change and sees improvement. "Thanks — responses restored"
Ryan (on-call): 10m after mitigation: error rate down to baseline. Preparing rollback to normal limits.
Ryan (on-call): rolling back RL: ```bash
redwood rl adjust --org planktonai --qps 100 --window 0m --reason "rollback after stabilization"
```
incident-bot: action-log: rl.adjust executed by ryan ; org=planktonai ; from=300 ; to=100 ; window=0m ; id=rl-act-7613
Maya (eng-sre): re-enabling streaming: ```bash
redwood ff set planktonai.streaming true --actor maya --note "restore after spike"
```
incident-bot: ff.update applied ; planktonai.streaming=true ; actor=maya ; id=ff-3850
Liz (ops): Marking as mitigated. Will capture traffic pattern and client signature for follow-up.
Ana (support): Updating CS ticket CS-8243 with mitigation actions and next steps.
Ryan (on-call): Filing follow-up task: ENG-OPS-1427 to investigate root cause (client retry behavior vs client-side bug) and to add automated soft-throttle that scales more gradually.
Maya (eng-sre): Also recommend a short postmortem with planktonai account team. I'll add logs and a waterfall of requests.
Ryan (on-call): Thanks all. Quiet now. Closing incident in 30m unless it resurfaces. :thumbsup:
Liz (ops): FYI metrics snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/metrics?org=planktonai&window=1h
Ana (support): Customer follow-up scheduled with AE tomorrow.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: planktonai surge mitigated; duration 00:25:20; actions: rl.adjust x2, ff toggle x2, qos.apply ; ticket=INC-1768500123
